plan: Given my value is $31, I want to win if the second highest bid is below $31. I need to consider the potential bids of Betty and Charles. Since this is round 1, there's no history. To maximize profit, I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the others might bid, but stay under my value. I'll bid $20. This minimizes potential loss if someone else overvalues the item. The worst case is I lose and pay nothing.

My value is $6. I want to win only if the price is very low. Given it's a single round, I'll bid slightly above $0 to try and secure the item cheaply, but avoid overpaying. I'll bid $0.10. This minimizes potential loss. If someone bids higher, I lose nothing. If I win, I win at a very low cost.

My value is $0. Since the prize is only worth $0 to me, I want to avoid paying anything. The worst-case scenario is bidding too high and winning, thus paying a price greater than my value (which is impossible since my value is 0). Therefore, I should bid as low as possible to avoid winning, but not so low that I automatically lose. A bid of $0.1 is the lowest possible and might win if the others bid similarly low.
